x402-overlap.title: How Autonomous Agents Pay for APIs With x402
x402-overlap.body:
With x402, an autonomous program can buy access to a web resource and skip signup, keys, and recurring plans. Coinbase introduced x402 in 2025 to turn the long-reserved HTTP 402 Payment Required status code into a working payment standard. Governance of the specification now sits with the x402 Foundation, a neutral body that Cloudflare helped launch.

An x402 server answers an unpaid request with a 402 response that lists what the client has to pay. Each payment requirement names a network, an asset, a payTo address, and the maximum amount required. The signed payment payload travels in the X-PAYMENT header of the retried request, in base64 encoding. After settlement succeeds, the server returns the resource together with an X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE header.

Payments in x402 settle in stablecoins, and USDC is the most common asset. Base, the Ethereum layer-two network developed by Coinbase, is the main network for x402 payments. The x402 protocol also supports payments on the Solana network in addition to EVM chains. Developers try out x402 flows on the Base Sepolia test network with free test tokens.

Because the facilitator covers the blockchain gas fee, the paying client does not have to hold a native gas token. Verification through a facilitator checks a payload against the requirements and never broadcasts an on-chain transaction. Even an untrustworthy facilitator is able to withhold settlement or stall a payment for an extended period.

The x402 reference implementation is published as open source under the Apache 2.0 license on GitHub. Middleware packages for Express and Hono add an x402 paywall to an existing route with a few lines of configuration. Model Context Protocol servers can wrap their tools in x402 so that an AI assistant pays per tool call.

Per-call overhead falls under batching, since a single blockchain transaction takes the place of many individual transfers. Batched settlement delays the final payment confirmation, so the seller carries credit risk during the batching window. If one payment inside a batch fails, the batch must be retried or split so the remaining payments are not blocked.

A proposed upto scheme lets a server charge any amount up to a signed maximum, which suits metered usage such as LLM tokens. Some sellers raise the quoted price in their 402 response when demand on an endpoint spikes. Refunds are outside the core protocol, so a seller who wants to refund must send a separate transfer back to the payer.

Every authorization carries a random nonce, which stops the token contract from accepting a replayed copy. The x402 Bazaar is a discovery catalog where agents can find paid endpoints to call. A typical safeguard is a cap per request that refuses any payment requirement exceeding a configured amount. Allowlists of approved seller domains stop an agent from paying unknown or malicious endpoints. Daily and monthly budgets protect an agent wallet from loops that keep calling a paid endpoint.

fresh-topic.title: CRDTs for Local-First Apps
fresh-topic.body: A conflict-free replicated data type is a data structure that merges concurrent edits from different replicas without coordination. CRDTs guarantee that replicas converge to the same state once every replica has received every update. Local-first software keeps the primary copy of user data on the user device and syncs the data in the background. Martin Kleppmann and coauthors described the local-first idea in a 2019 essay from the Ink and Switch research lab. Automerge and Yjs are open-source libraries that implement CRDTs for collaborative documents. A grow-only counter CRDT stores one count per replica and computes the total by summing all counts. Text CRDTs assign a unique identifier to each character so that concurrent inserts keep a consistent order. Deleted items in many CRDTs remain as tombstones, which makes document history grow over time.
